name: German Bread
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: milk well boiled
ingredients.originalText: one pint of milk well boiled

ingredients.name: two tablespoonfuls of nice lard or butter
ingredients.originalText: two tablespoonfuls of nice lard or butter
ingredients.quantityText: two tablespoonfuls of nice lard or butter

ingredients.name: two-thirds of a teacupful of baker's yeast
ingredients.originalText: two-thirds of a teacupful of baker's yeast

instructions.text: Make a rising with the milk and yeast
when light, mix in the sugar and shortening with flour enough to make as soft a dough as can be handled
Flour the paste-board well and roll out about one-half inch thick
put this quantity into two large pans
make about a dozen indentures with the finger on the top
put a small piece of butter in each and sift over the whole one tablespoonful of sugar mixed with one teaspoonful of cinnamon
Let this stand for a second rising
when perfectly light, bake in a quick oven fifteen or twenty minutes

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Make a rising with the milk and yeast
2. when light, mix in the sugar and shortening with flour enough to make as soft a dough as can be handled
3. Flour the paste-board well and roll out about one-half inch thick
4. put this quantity into two large pans
5. make about a dozen indentures with the finger on the top
6. put a small piece of butter in each and sift over the whole one tablespoonful of sugar mixed with one teaspoonful of cinnamon
7. Let this stand for a second rising
8. when perfectly light, bake in a quick oven fifteen or twenty minutes
